answer: Anchor one identity per person to physical encounters. An applicant's phone collects signed Bluetooth proofs from five unrelated, long-standing members met at different public places over 30 days, such as a wharf market and a mesa-top park; each proof binds the epoch seed so it cannot be replayed. Forging a fake costs real travel plus five accomplices, scaling linearly per fake, and encounter graphs expose clusters sharing few witnesses. Limits: rural users meet fewer witnesses and staged meetups can be bought, so lagoon towns get longer windows and witness rings face audits and slashing.
